payload.name: Preserve Distinct Relations During Memory Enrichment
payload.description: During construction UPDATE/enrichment, if the candidate expresses a different relation about the subject than the existing memory (e.g., recommends/suggests vs. likes/owns), use the relation explicitly or add a separate memory. Do not absorb the new fact into the old relation.
content: During UPDATE/enrichment, compare the relation in the candidate content with the relation in the target memory (e.g., 'recommends to' vs. 'enjoys').

If the relations differ, do not merge by rewriting the candidate into the old predicate. Keep the new relation explicit—enrich the memory with a clause like 'recommends X to Y' or create a separate memory for the recommendation.
Only merge new items into the existing relation when the new evidence expresses the same predicate (e.g., more titles the person enjoys).

candidates.solves: The failure occurs when an UPDATE merges a candidate with a distinct relation (e.g., recommends/suggests) into an existing memory with a different relation (e.g., likes/owns), so the new relation is lost. This Skill applies in future sessions where a speaker recommends specific items while an earlier memory records the same speaker's preferences; preserve the recommendation relation explicitly. It does not apply when new evidence only adds more instances of the same existing relation.

payload.name: Preserve preference purpose across extraction and updates
payload.description: Use when creating or updating a memory for a user's stated preference/plan that includes an explicit purpose ('so that', 'to', 'because', 'in order to'); preserve both preference and purpose and avoid overwriting it with unrelated updates.
content: When a statement contains a preference and an explicit purpose clause, extract the preference and the purpose as one memory object; do not emit a candidate that only repeats the surface preference.

During CRUD, before rewriting an existing memory that captures a durable preference, check whether the incoming message is about a different topic; if it is, ADD a new memory instead of UPDATE or MERGE, so the original preference and its purpose remain available.
Only preserve purposes that are explicit in the message; a time or place modifier alone is not a purpose, so do not fabricate one.

candidates.solves: When a stated preference is recorded without its explicit reason, or later overwritten by an unrelated update, motivation questions cannot be answered. Apply when a user statement pairs a preference/plan with an explicit purpose ('so that', 'to', 'because') and when updating an older preference memory with unrelated new information. Do not apply when no purpose is stated, and never invent a reason absent from the evidence.

payload.name: Preserve recommendation claims when enriching preference memories
payload.description: When constructing memories and a candidate contains an explicit recommendation, offer, or suggestion that overlaps an existing memory of only personal enjoyment/preference, use this Skill to ensure the recommendation claim is preserved.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly recommends, suggests, or offers items to someone, capture the recommendation as a distinct claim, not merely as the speaker's enjoyment or preference.

During UPDATE/MERGE, if the candidate includes a recommendation claim and the existing target memory only records the subject's personal enjoyment/preference for those same items, do not collapse the recommendation into enjoyment. Preserve the recommendation claim in the updated memory content (e.g., 'recommends ... to ...') or create a separate relationship/event memory for the recommendation. Ensure the updated content explicitly states that the subject recommended the items, not just that they like or play them.

candidates.solves: Construction updates often collapse an explicit recommendation into a generic enjoyment/preference memory when the target already covers the same items, so future questions about recommendations fail. Use when a construction candidate contains an expressed recommendation, offer, or suggestion that overlaps an existing preference/enjoyment memory; preserve the recommendation claim in the updated memory or a separate relationship memory. Do not apply when new evidence only reinforces enjoyment without any recommendation, or when adding unrelated new facts.

payload.name: Preserve recommendation context when enriching memories
payload.description: When a construction candidate contains an explicit recommendation or suggestion about a topic already captured as a preference, apply this during CRUD to keep the recommendation verb and qualifier in the memory instead of converting it to a generic enjoyment statement.
content: During CRUD, when a candidate contains an explicit recommendation or suggestion (e.g., 'recommends X', 'suggested X as Y') and the target existing memory describes the same topic as a preference or enjoyment, preserve the recommendation verb and any qualifier in the updated memory; do not rewrite it as only 'enjoys' or 'likes'.

If the existing memory already captures the same entity as a preference, either create a separate event memory for the recommendation (subject = speaker, content = 'recommended X as Y') or explicitly include 'recommended' in the updated content, so the source's suggestion remains retrievable.
Do not apply when the source message only states what someone plays, likes, or does without an explicit recommendation; such statements may still be merged as preference enrichments.

candidates.solves: Construction CRUD sometimes loses recommendation context when enriching an existing preference memory, turning 'recommends X as Y' into 'enjoys X'. This Skill applies when a candidate explicitly records a recommendation and an existing memory about the same topic is updated; it preserves the recommendation verb and qualifier, or creates a separate recommendation event. It does not apply when the source only states an activity or preference without any explicit recommendation.
